snippet.description:
Horse racing can be an unusually dangerous profession for both the jockey and the horse: Riding a half-ton animal at nearly 40 miles per hour means your fate depends on the health and performance of both athletes. And the horse can be at risk of catastrophic injury if the jockey doesn’t have the required physical fitness to maintain proper technique and lightning-quick reflexes. 

In order to find out more about keeping both of these athletes healthy, Vox producer Nate Krieger took a trip to Belmont Park to watch competitive horses train and to speak with Dr. Sara Langsam, an equine veterinarian and chair of the American Association of Equine Practitioners Racing Committee.

What does an 8-year UPSC journey actually look like?

AIR 100 Sattwik Satyakam Devta sits down with LevelUp IAS to talk about the attempts, setbacks, decisions and lessons that shaped his journey from starting UPSC preparation in 2018 to securing AIR 100.

From leaving a job at Maruti Suzuki to preparing alongside his NABARD career, Sattwik shares what changed in his final attempt, how he approached answer writing and revision, how he used AI, and why he stopped believing that preparation means cutting yourself off from everything else.

snippet.description:
One Source Is Better Than 100 UPSC Notes.

In this video, AIR 87 Sayali Bhika Pagar (UPSC CSE 2025) and LevelUp IAS Mains Master Program student shares an important lesson about using Telegram notes and multiple UPSC study sources.

With endless notes and materials available online, many aspirants keep switching from one source to another. Sayali explains why source-hopping can create confusion and how aspirants can evaluate different sources before choosing one reliable source and sticking to it consistently.

For UPSC CSE preparation, repeated revision of one source is often more useful than continuously collecting new notes and materials.

One Source Is Better Than 100 UPSC Notes.

In this video, AIR 87 Sayali Bhika Pagar (UPSC CSE 2025) and LevelUp IAS Mains Master Program student shares an important lesson about using Telegram notes and multiple UPSC study sources.

With endless notes and materials available online, many aspirants keep switching from one source to another. Sayali explains why source-hopping can create confusion and how aspirants can evaluate different sources before choosing one reliable source and sticking to it consistently.

For UPSC CSE preparation, repeated revision of one source is often more useful than continuously collecting new notes and materials.
